correctness.rationale: For odd q, set D=A−B, so A=(C+D)/2 and B=(C−D)/2. Their conditions are equivalent to D*=D, CD+DC=0 and D²=−C². Different eigenspaces of the split selfadjoint C are orthogonal and each is nondegenerate. The anticommutation equation forces D to map V_λ into V_{−λ}; for λ nonzero the equation on D² makes the map invertible, so an unpaired eigenspace or unequal dimensions are impossible. On a paired block write D's upper-right entry as λT; selfadjointness gives the lower-left as λT*, and the square condition is T*T=−I and TT*=−I. This is exactly an anti-isometry of the two forms. The two determinant square classes must agree after negation of one form; this is exactly the stated character test. The valid maps form one torsor under the orthogonal group of the plus-labelled eigenspace. The kernels of C±D are graphs over one m_λ-dimensional eigenspace, so each summand has rank m_λ there. On V_0, B_0=−A_0; a square-zero selfadjoint A_0 has isotropic image U and kernel U^⊥, and the canonical identification V_0/U^⊥≅U* gives a bijection with nonsingular symmetric maps U*→U. The isotropic-line count from the finite-field quadratic zero count and quotienting by a hyperbolic plane multiply to count complete isotropic flags, then division by the flags in an r-plane gives I_r. The stabilizers of the two congruence classes relative to GL_r give S_r, with the stated orders and Witt signs. All factors are positive on the stated support, with the empty, zero-dimensional and rank-zero conventions consistent. The choices are ordered, so swapping A and B does not call for division by two. The independent replay directly tested all 59049 selfadjoint 4×4 matrices in each of four F3 cases and found 1+32z+144z², 2z+8z², 8z² and 0, checking both ranks. The replay is not a test of all odd q or of the recorded extension-field sample; the proof covers arbitrary odd q in the split setting.

value.rationale: Existence does not determine the multiplicities of decompositions, even for invertible targets. The result supplies a fixed-target finite-field enumeration, separates the dependence on eigenspace form types from the nilpotent freedom on the zero eigenspace, and gives the attained ranks and their exact weights. The nonzero-block torsor count and its rank contribution address a natural gap beyond the earlier existence theorem and the known zero-target count.
